A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite the changed title and substantial reorganization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison; retained material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments measuring optimizer loss, gradients, margins, and correlations with maximum-margin classifiers in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v4 reports original synthetic-data experiments and MNIST neural-network experiments in Figures 1–4, alongside retained Adam experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: v4 introduces normalized momentum steepest descent into the studied algorithmic family: updates maximize alignment with an exponential moving average of gradients over a norm ball (Equations 4–5). This adds Signum, NMD-GD, and an EMA-based Muon procedure; the existing NSD and Adam procedures remain.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates synthetic separable multiclass data with linear classifiers. v4 retains this coverage and adds MNIST digit classification with a two-layer neural network, substantially extending the empirical domain and nonlinear test setting.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated comparisons involving Muon, Signum, and NMD-GD, while removing the Nuclear-GD comparisons from v2 Figure 3. The NGD, SignGD, and Adam comparison remains in Appendix G.

E3.justification: The main spectral experiment changes from 10 to 50 samples per class and from a learning-rate prefactor of 0.01 to 0.05; v4 uses 0.1 for SignGD and NGD. The new MNIST protocol specifies 100 examples per class, 100 hidden units, first-layer-only versus joint training, and two spectral-margin definitions.

E4.justification: v4 Figure 3 adds a controlled comparison of first-layer-only and joint-layer training to examine norm preferences in nonlinear networks. The existing Adam stability-constant sensitivity analysis is retained in Appendix G, Figures 5–6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run summaries, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting, but introduces no new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v4 adds momentum-method margin and correlation curves and MNIST spectral-margin trajectories, while removing Nuclear-GD and nuclear-separator results. Changed synthetic settings prevent interpreting the new curves as same-setting improvements. Adam's two-phase finding and reference margins of 2.11 and 17.83 remain in Figures 5–6.

T1.justification: v4 adds NMD convergence Theorems 2 and 4, stating an O((d log t + dn)/sqrt(t)) margin-gap rate, with momentum-error bounds and proofs in Appendix E. Existing NSD and Adam rates are retained through reorganization. The new Appendix E derivation contains inconsistent bookkeeping of factors of d.

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds SignGD and Adam's max-norm bias alongside general NSD results. v4 makes NSD/NMD characterization, particularly Spectral-GD and Muon, its central contribution and adds a claim about nonlinear norm-preference behavior. Adam's claim remains as an extension.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the MNIST results as evidence that linear norm preferences can persist in nonlinear networks. It identifies NMD's feature-dimension dependence as a limitation and distinguishes its EMA-style Muon analysis from the cited Nesterov implementation. The Adam stability-constant interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v4 newly identifies CVXPY for reference-margin computation, explicitly documents truncated SVD in experiments, and describes the sigmoid network. Its checklist states that supplemental code is provided, which cannot be verified from these PDFs. Conversely, the relocated Adam study no longer supplies v2's explicit learning-rate prefactor.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning around LLM optimizers and Muon scaling and convergence research. Remark 1 qualifies v2's spectral-descent novelty positioning against the updated Tsilivis work, emphasizing discrete normalized updates, momentum, and non-asymptotic rates rather than gradient-flow KKT convergence.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are rewritten around Spectral Descent and Muon. The separate SignGD/general-NSD exposition is consolidated, related work moves after experiments, and Adam's main discussion moves into Appendix G. The appendices are reorganized and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v4 adds the algorithm/rate summary table and momentum/MNIST figures, replaces the nuclear-descent figure, and relocates Adam figures to the appendix. Figure 6 removes the zoomed gradient panel but retains an outdated five-panel caption.

improvement.justification: The NMD/Muon analysis and dedicated empirical checks substantially extend v2's explanation of optimizer bias to normalized momentum methods. The unified exposition and MNIST layer-training comparisons strengthen its explanatory and empirical reach. These gains outweigh the loss of Nuclear-GD validation and local defects, including Appendix E's inconsistent d factors, reduced Adam-setting disclosure, and Figure 6's outdated caption.
